To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) variable-rate application of nitrogen is more profitable on fields with high spatial variability in potential yield, 2) variable-rate application decreases nitrogen losses, and 3) the benefits of variable-rate application are greater in the presence of low uncertainty about potential yields.

variable-rate nitrogen application can reduce nitrogen losses, increase profits, and increase yield stability, but the magnitude of the benefits depends on the level of yield variability and uncertainty about potential yields.
the economic benefits of variable-rate nitrogen applications depend on the extent of uncertainty about potential yield and that variable-rate applications reduce nitrogen use.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the economic and environmental implications of variable-rate nitrogen applications under uncertainty.
the economic and environmental impacts of site-specific nitrogen application.
the value of information and the value of variable application.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the value of sitespecific technologies is higher when the spatial variability is high, the potential yield distribution is positively skewed, the yield to nitrogen response is high, and uncertainty is low.
the value of site specific information and variable rate application depends upon the nature of the field and its potential yields.

the value of variable rate application is greater than uniform application in most cases, but that the extent of the difference is sensitive to uncertainty about yields and the responsiveness of yields to nitrogen.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the economic benefits of variable-rate nitrogen are substantial, especially for low-yield, high-variability fields.

variable rate nitrogen application can be economically and environmentally beneficial but that the extent of the benefit is sensitive to yield uncertainty and the degree of over-application of nitrogen.

the value of variable rate application depends on the level of uncertainty about potential yield and the extent of spatial variability in potential yield, as well as the responsiveness of yield to nitrogen, the price of nitrogen and the price of yield.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the value of variable nitrogen application is not uniform across the farm.
uncertainty about yields is an important determinant of the value of variable rate nitrogen application.
variable-rate technologies are not a panacea.
